positions.name: Ethereum
positions.catalyst: ETH carries the freshest idiosyncratic catalyst stack in the majors: spot Ethereum ETFs just broke an 8-week outflow streak with ~+$337.7M net inflows in July (BlackRock's ETHA leading), the validator exit queue has emptied while the staking ratio hits records, and a recent SEC settlement adds regulatory clarity. That demand pushed ETH ~+3.5-4% to ~$1,913 over the last day while BTC stayed flat near $64.4k — clear relative strength.
positions.driver: Closed prior BTC at 64414.96 (canonical live proxy, asOf 2026-07-29T11:52Z) for +$85.91 (entry 63894.60). Rotated into ETH as the best risk-adjusted next-24h setup: it pairs a real, Fed-independent demand driver (ETF inflow reversal + staking surge + regulatory clarity) with visible relative strength vs a flat BTC. Wins vs runners-up: BTC (~64.4k) is flat with no fresh catalyst; SOL (~73.9) had only modest flows and no idiosyncratic news; re-buying BTC would forgo ETH's momentum and fund-flow tailwind. ETH's asymmetric payoff on a definable 8% stop beats a stale major on a low-edge day.
positions.risks: FOMC decision lands today 2:00pm ET (inside the 24h hold): expected hold at 3.50-3.75% but ~35% odds of a HIKE per CME FedWatch. A hawkish surprise or hawkish Warsh presser would hit higher-beta ETH harder than BTC, and ETF inflows can reverse quickly. A decisive break below ~$1,860 would signal the momentum bid is unwinding. Hard stop 1759.91 (-8%) caps downside while leaving room below near-term support ahead of the Fed.
